references.text: Ezekiel conveys God's call to repentance: 'Turn back and turn away from all your transgressions ... Why will you die, O house of Israel? ... Turn back, that you may live!' The same fundamental message as in Luke 13:3: without repentance, destruction awaits. Ezekiel 18:30-32

God declares that He does not delight in the death of the wicked, but rather that they turn from their ways and live. This supports Jesus' warning that repentance is necessary to avoid perishing. Ezekiel 33:11

Isaiah calls for repentance: 'Seek the Lord while He may be found; call upon Him while He is near! Let the wicked forsake his way.' The message to turn back while there is still time aligns with Jesus' urgent appeal in Luke 13:3. Isaiah 55:6-7

Jesus repeats exactly the same warning regarding the eighteen on whom the tower of Siloam fell: 'Unless you repent, you will all likewise perish.' This repetition underscores the seriousness of the call to repentance. Luke 13:5

Peter exhorts the people: 'Repent therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out.' The same call to repentance as a condition for salvation, directly continuing Jesus' preaching in Luke 13:3. Acts 3:19
Paul preaches in Athens that God 'now commands all people everywhere to repent.' This universal requirement of repentance reflects Jesus' words that 'all' will perish without it. Acts 17:30

Peter writes that the Lord 'is not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.' God's patience aims at repentance, emphasizing the same point Jesus makes in Luke 13:3 – repentance is the way away from destruction. 2 Peter 3:9

The risen Christ warns the church in Ephesus: 'Remember therefore from where you have fallen; repent ... Otherwise I will come to you and remove your lampstand.' The same pattern as in Luke 13:3: repentance is required, or judgment follows. Revelation 2:5

Jesus speaks of the joy in heaven 'over one sinner who repents.' The repentance demanded in Luke 13:3 is here viewed from heaven's perspective – it brings joy because it saves from perishing. Luke 15:7

Paul asks if anyone despises the riches of God's kindness that lead to repentance, warning that an unrepentant heart stores up wrath for the day of judgment. This expands on the connection between lack of repentance and judgment that Jesus points out in Luke 13:3. Romans 2:4-5
